title: finance-budget-1on1-prep
content:
Meeting: 1:1 prep - Finance run-rate + procurement review (with CFO)
Owner: Jordan Lee
Date of meeting: 2026-03-04 (prep notes for 2026-03-05 sync)
Context: quick sync to review current run-rate burn, upcoming procurement approvals (infra and data annotation), and ask for decision on procurement cap increase + hiring freeze exceptions. Keep it short (20-30 min).

Agenda draft:
- 5m: Quick status update (run-rate summary + headcount impacts)
- 10m: Procurement approvals (list items + ask)
- 5m: Near-term cost mitigations and risks (autoscaling, reserved vs on-demand, pause non-critical infra)
- 5m: Action items / decisions / next steps

Key numbers (as of Feb close):
- Monthly run-rate (spend): $285,000/month (~$3.42M annualized)
- Core infra (GPU instances, infra ops): $125k/mo (44% of spend)
- Third-party services (embedding API, monitoring, data labeling): $68k/mo (24%)
- Payroll + benefits: $75k/mo (26%)
- Other (licenses, travel, misc): $17k/mo (6%)
- YTD variance vs plan: +8% (over plan by ~$22k/mo) — driven by extra annotation spend and a burst of cloud testing in Jan

Top procurement items to surface (need CFO sign-off / approval):
1) Dedicated GPU reserved nodes (Q2 reserved capacity contract)
   - Ask: Approve $480k annual contract (committed) vs continued on-demand spend (projected $620k/yr currently for same QPS)
   - Note: Break-even ~9 months given current utilization; assumes we can maintain Q2-Q4 throughput.
   - Risk: If we drop throughput, we can request downgrade but contract terms require 60 days notice.

2) Data annotation vendor (quality ramp for new NLU evals)
   - Ask: Approve $120k one-time for Q2 labeling batch (covers ~100k units)
   - Note: This is mostly one-off to improve eval coverage and reduce model regressions; reduces ongoing human-in-loop costs if we pair with semi-auto tooling.

3) Monitoring/log retention tier increase
   - Ask: Approve $18k/yr to extend retention from 30 -> 90 days for cost/latency trace debugging (critical for rollouts)

Key questions I want to get answers to in the meeting:
- Which procurement items should be prioritized if we only get partial approval? (my priority: 1) reserved GPU nodes, 2) labeling batch, 3) retention increase)
- Are we comfortable converting $480k to a committed contract given uncertain Q3 demand? Any suggested guardrails?
- Do we have appetite to extend hiring exceptions for two infra hires (SRE + infra eng) if we approve reserved capacity? Cost impact ~ $22k/mo combined fully loaded.

Quick mitigation proposals (if CFO pushes back):
- Defer labeling batch to Q3 and cut $120k (saves $120k now, but slows eval improvements)
- Move reserved capacity to 6-month rolling if vendor supports (request shorter term or step-down)
- Cap non-prod GPU bursts by applying a daily quota and schedule heavy tests to off-hours (saves ~15-20% of infra spikes)

Open items I need to finish before meeting:
- Reconcile Feb card spend: need line-items for the extra $22k over plan (tickets: JIRA-BUDGET-87) — ACTION: Alex to pull vendor invoices and line items by 2026-03-03
- Prepare a 1-slide ROI calculation for reserved GPUs (show break-even and sensitivity to +/-20% throughput) — ACTION: Jordan to draft by 2026-03-04 EOD
- Confirm label vendor SLAs and sample outputs for PO attachment — ACTION: Priya to get samples by 2026-03-04

Proposed draft ask language for CFO (short):
"Requesting approval for a Q2 reserved GPU commit of $480k and a one-time $120k labeling batch. The reserved commit reduces expected infra cost by ~$140k/year at current utilization and improves latency predictability for product rollouts. If full approval is not feasible, recommend prioritizing the reserved GPU commit and deferring labeling."

Follow-up / action items table (informal):
- Alex Kim: Provide detailed Feb card spend breakdown (due 2026-03-03)
- Jordan Lee: ROI slide for reserved GPUs + sensitivity analysis (due 2026-03-04 EOD)
- Priya Kapoor: Label vendor sample pack and SLA (due 2026-03-04)
- Finance Ops (cc): Prepare PO template for $600k+ approvals (in case both asks approved)

Notes to self / talking points (shorthand):
- Emphasize cost-savings vs on-demand, but be honest about utilization risk
- Tie labeling to reduction in model regressions (have a 2-3 example bug slips to cite)
- If CFO asks about runway: remind that burn + hires implies runway at current spend ~9 months w/ current cash (high-level only)
- Keep the ask concise, avoid technical deep-dives unless asked

Unresolved questions / follow-ups after meeting:
- If reserved commit denied, re-run forecast with 15% lower infra spend and produce Q2 contingency plan (ACTION if denied)
- Confirm procurement threshold and who signs $500k+ PO (legal?) — linked artifact? (Procure ticket PR-4521)

End of notes.

Draft version history: initial notes 2026-02-26 by Jordan Lee; updated with numbers after Feb close 2026-03-02.
